subject: Fit a model having continuous variables and categorical variable

messages.author: 9722eb2c3ef2de41
messages.subject: Fit a model having continuous variables and categorical variable
parts:
Hi everyone, I am now fitting a model in which there are two factors which correlate each other (factor1 ~ factor2). For more details, you can see my model as following: model1<- 'factor1=~ind1 + ind2 + ind3 factor2=~ind4 + ind5 + ind6 + ind7 + ind8 factor1~factor2' My problem is that ind1, ind2, ind3 are continuous variables (a six-point Likert scale) while ind4, ind5, ind6, ind7, ind8 are category variables (a 3 point-Likert scale). However I do not know which estimator I should use to fit my model. Could anyone show me which estimator that best fit for my model?

Thanks you all ;)
Carlos

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Fit a model having continuous variables and categorical variable
parts: Could anyone show me which estimator that best fit for my model?

When you have any categorical outcomes (regardless of whether you also have continuous outcomes), tell lavaan() or cfa() which variables are ordered and lavaan will automatically use the appropriate estimator: diagonally weighted least squares (DWLS) with a robust correction for SEs and test statistics (look in the right column of the summary() output).

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html
